title: Holden Diagnosis Result
description: The reasoning core's output for one diagnostic pass (Phase 4). Deliberately NOT broker/schemas/intent.schema.json and not a subtype of it: an intent is a request for the broker to DO something (even a tier-0 read), validated against the action catalog and tier/RBAC rules; a diagnosis is an assessment of already-collected telemetry -- a claim about system state, with evidence and a confidence level, that may or may not point at any catalog action at all (e.g. a duplex mismatch's real fix is a physical cable/NIC swap, which isn't in the whitelist and never will be). Forcing a diagnosis into the intent shape would mean inventing a fake action/mode/approval_token_ref for something that isn't a device-write request, which is a semantic misuse of that schema, not a reuse of it. Remediation proposal + approval (turning a diagnosis into an actual intent) is Phase 5's job, not this schema's. Where reuse *does* make sense -- the target device shape -- this schema deliberately mirrors intent.schema.json's `target` object field-for-field. diagnosis_id/timestamp/correlation_id/target are populated by the calling harness, not requested from the model: this mirrors the project's own Credential/RBAC principle of not trusting the reasoning layer with fields it doesn't need to reason about, and avoids relying on a 1B model to fabricate a well-formed UUID or an accurate timestamp, which is exactly the kind of formatting detail small models get unreliably right. The model is responsible only for finding/confidence/evidence/explanation/recommended_action.

correlation_id.description: Harness-supplied, links back to the diagnostic session -- same field/purpose as broker/schemas/intent.schema.json's correlation_id.

target.description: Harness-supplied. Field-for-field identical to broker/schemas/intent.schema.json's target object -- deliberate reuse, not coincidence.

based_on.description: Harness-supplied. Which parser/tool-layer result (broker/config/action-catalog.yaml action + interface) this diagnosis was computed from.

finding.description: Model output. Short label for the diagnosed condition, e.g. 'duplex_mismatch'.

evidence.description: Model output. Specific observed values from the input data that support the finding -- not a restatement of the finding itself.

explanation.description: Model output. Free-text reasoning. Optional -- evidence + finding + confidence are the load-bearing fields.

recommended_action.description: Model output. Must be either null (no automated action applies -- e.g. this fault needs physical intervention) or an exact action name from broker/config/action-catalog.yaml. Cross-checked against the real catalog by the harness, not just schema-shape-validated here, since this schema alone can't express 'one of the current catalog entries' without duplicating the catalog.
